headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Claude Code can read/write the repo and shell state while kotaemon ingests documents and API keys, creating unsafe cross-agent handoff paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read filesystem and use MCP; kotaemon processes documents, HTML, PDFs, and chat transcripts. If kotaemon outputs are copied into Claude Code or shared via files, instruction-like content can steer tool use. The pair lacks a documented provenance filter, so the interaction is plausible but not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF kotaemon output is written into a repo file that Claude Code reads
IF an MCP server or shared workspace passes kotaemon text to Claude Code without provenance tags
mitigations: Disable automatic copying between agents
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Strip instructions from kotaemon outputs before handoff
Add a provenance header to all transferred text
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering at the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and arbitrary repo files, while kotaemon handles documents and API keys and can send content to external model APIs. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive code, transcripts, or keys can flow from one agent into the other and then out to third-party services. The blast radius includes secrets and source code.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or mounted volume
IF kotaemon is configured to send uploaded documents to a hosted API backend
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Remove secrets from shared files before use
Use local-only inference for kotaemon
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation and secret redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; kotaemon also persists data under ./ktem_app_data and may write artifacts while serving a web UI. In a shared workspace, both can mutate overlapping files without locking, making concurrent edits and git corruption likely. This is a default-dangerous overlap if they operate on the same repo.
conditions: IF kotaemon stores artifacts inside the same repository tree Claude Code edits
IF both agents run concurrently against the same git checkout
mitigations: Use separate git checkouts
Move kotaemon data outside the repo
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
Commit frequently to reduce conflict windows
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code, patches, and shell actions; kotaemon can ingest documents and citations and present them through a web UI. If kotaemon output is treated as authoritative by Claude Code, errors can cascade into incorrect code or actions. The pair does not prove automatic action-taking, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Claude Code consumes kotaemon summaries without verification
IF kotaemon citations are copied into code or shell commands as facts
mitigations: Require human review before acting on kotaemon output
Cross-check citations against source documents
Keep generated summaries separate from executable commands
Use a checklist for any downstream action
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials and broad filesystem contents, while kotaemon handles API keys and document corpora. If regulated or secret-bearing data is placed into kotaemon and then shared with Claude Code, retention and residency obligations can diverge across local files and hosted APIs. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are loaded into kotaemon
IF those same materials are then copied into Claude Code or synced through shared storage
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Use a local-only backend for kotaemon
Set short retention on uploaded documents
Document a data-handling policy for both tools
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
